replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not really. My high neuroticism score might make me overthink, but I've learned to break problems into small steps. When stressed, I meditate or hike—activities that help me stay calm and focused on the math.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used AI tools to practice algebra and calculus. They provided instant feedback and step-by-step solutions, which helped me understand concepts faster. I felt more confident than before, though I still prefer hands-on practice.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; zero, one solution; negative, complex. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a) to find the roots.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug the x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points could be maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
